headlines.title: Forward progress stopped on vegetation fire in South San Jose
headlines.description: Firefighters were battling a vegetation fire in South San Jose on Saturday. At 12:05 p.m., Cal Fire SCU said on X the blaze was reported in the 9500 block of Malech Road in South San Jose, near the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office shooting range. Initially, the fire had burned 3 acres, but it later grew to 25 acres, authorities said. At 1:19 p.m., Cal Fire reported the forward progress of the fire was stopped, and the flames ended up burning 32 acres. headlines.title: 49ers icon Roger Craig shares vascular dementia diagnosis in Hall of Fame speech
headlines.description: Legendary running back Roger Craig made a startling disclosure Saturday during his pre-recorded acceptance speech into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Toward the end of his 10-minute address, Craig revealed he has been diagnosed with vascular dementia. Vascular dementia, the second-most common dementia diagnosis behind Alzheimer’s, is caused by conditions that limit blood flow to the brain and can lead to problems with memory, thinking, and behavior. Craig, 66, played 11 seasons in the NFL from 1983 to ’93. He played for the 49ers during his first eight seasons as a professional. “Today, there is another chapter I want to share,” Craig said in his remarks that were played at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton, Ohio, and broadcast to a national-television audience. “I’ve been diagnosed with vascular dementia that my doctors believe may be related, at least in part, to the concussions I experienced during my career.” Craig had not spoken publicly since his election was announced as one of the five-person Class of 2026 on Feb. 5 during the NFL Honors show at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco. Craig said his condition worsened gradually over time and was initially dismissed as normal aging. He spoke candidly about the dichotomy between all football gave him and the potential risks of playing the game. “Two things could be true,” Craig said. “Football gave me opportunities beyond anything I can imagine. It helped shape the man I became. At the same time, we know more today about brain health than when I played. And I hope sharing my story encourages people to pay attention to their health and seek help when something doesn’t feel right.” Craig exhibited all of the positive attributes that made him one of the 49ers’ most popular players at a time when both sides of the ball were stacked with other star players. “I want people to know this diagnosis doesn’t define me,” he said. “I am still Roger Craig. I am still a father, a husband, a teammate, a friend, and someone who loves this game, and the people who brought it to my life. “If sharing my story helps even one family or one former player, then it’s worth it. Football gave me everything: Opportunity, discipline, lifelong friends, and the platform to grow as a man.” Download and follow the 49ers Talk Podcast

headlines.title: Heat advisory and coastal flood advisory issued for the Bay Area through Sunday
headlines.description: The National Weather Service issued a heat advisory Saturday for the interior Bay Area and Central Coast through Sunday night. The NWS also issued a coastal flood advisory for Bayshore locations through Thursday. High temperatures are forecast to be in the 90s and up to 105 degrees Fahrenheit in some interior parts of the region, according to the advisory. Lows are forecast to be in the 60s to 80s. The advisory was active in parts of all Bay Area and Central Coast counties from Monterey to Sonoma, except Marin County. Links to cooling centers or plans to operate them in each county are available through the California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services website. The Weather Service recommended avoiding strenuous outdoor activities, staying hydrated, and shifting outdoor labor to evening or morning hours when it will be cooler than midday. Pet owners should take precautions not to leave animals in vehicles. A coastal flood advisory was also issued for the Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San Pablo Bay and Monterey Bay through Thursday at 2 a.m., warning of high tides of up to 1.6 ft. and flooding of lots, parks and roads.
headlines.source: Bay City News and NBC Bay Area staff

headlines.title: Palo Alto quiet zone project near Caltrain crossings delayed
headlines.description: In Palo Alto, those living near Caltrain crossings will have to wait a bit longer before the train horns are quieted. The city has been trying to win “quiet zone” designations from the federal government at its four rail crossings. The project is now being delayed due to concerns of traffic congestion near or on the tracks. Normally, trains are required to blare their horns four times to signal their approach to crossing traffic; in quiet zones, there is no horn. Instead, more secure gates are installed to prevent cars, bikes and pedestrians from accessing the tracks when a train is passing.

headlines.title: Suisun City Council declares state of emergency after cyberattack
headlines.description: The Suisun City Council declared a state of emergency Saturday after a cyberattack that shut down computer systems including 911 public safety operations. “Malicious software infected and compromised” the East Bay community’s information technology systems beginning about 5:45 a.m. Friday, the city said on social media. “The cybersecurity incident hit critical public safety operations, including 911 routing, police and fire dispatch, records and city services,” the city said. “There is no imminent threat to the public,” the city said. “All public safety services remain active.” The city shut down its computer network “to contain the threat and preserve evidence for a federal investigation,” it said. The city, with a population of about 30,000, said it is working with the FBI, Department of Homeland Security and California Office of Emergency Services to investigate the incident and restore systems. The state of emergency, approved at a special meeting of the council Saturday morning, allows the city to access emergency support services and to recoup costs of the cybersecurity incident, it said. Suisun City dispatchers were taking calls for service through the Solano County dispatch center. Suisun City police officers and firefighters continued responding to calls for service, the city said, but online city services and internal operations were unavailable.

headlines.title: 2nd day of Outside Lands in SF: What is being done to ease traffic
headlines.description: Saturday was the second day of the Outside Lands Music Festival in San Francisco. To help ease traffic, attendees were advised not to drive to the festival, and the city offered extra Muni service and restricted Waymo pickups. It’s the 18th year of the Outside Lands, and 75,000 fans are expected each day of the sold-out three-day festival. Extra Muni service will run before and after the festival in addition to regular service. There are designated rideshare and taxi areas, autonomous vehicles are restricted to rides a few blocks away from the festival; the plan comes a month after a drivers were caught in late night traffic on the Fourth of July in the city. San Francisco Aug 7 concerts Aug 5 San Francisco Aug 4 Denise lives nearby and says the changes seem to be working. “I think it gets better and more efficient every year, it’s been fairly quiet, I don’t want to jinx it, however yeah it seems very organized as you can see its quite quiet I, would say the only time that it does get a little busy is when the concert ends around 9:30 p.m.-10 p.m.,” she said. Concertgoers definitely seemed to have a plan for getting out after the show, and neighbors say that’s when the real test is.

headlines.title: Man arrested in connection with deadly stabbing in Martinez
headlines.description: On Friday, an arrest was made in connection with a deadly stabbing in a Martinez neighborhood. Police say 36-year-old Marcos Iriarte-Valdez was arrested Friday night just before 6:30 p.m in Martinez. He’s facing murder charges in the death of 68-year-old Todd Stewart. Martinez police said that at around 5:00 p.m. on Thursday, the suspect drove up to Francis Court, a residential neighborhood in Martinez. In a photo provided by police, the suspect appears to arrive in a SUV and to be wearing tactical gear. “It appears that the suspect had pulled into a court — this is a large residential area, mostly single-family homes — pulled into there and at some point got into a confrontation with the victim,” said Martinez Police Chief Andrew White. “Our understanding was the victim was simply inside of their garage working, and that [confrontation] culminated with the victim being stabbed and the suspect fleeing the area,” he continued. White said that using surveillance video from neighbors and resources from multiple agencies, police were able to track down the vehicle and arrest Valdez. “It’s obviously deeply unsettling, it was a horrific attack with no known connection to the victim,” White noted, emphasizing that at this stage in the investigation police are not aware of any connection between Valdez and Stewart. White added that at this point, they do not know what Valdez’s motive may have been. Martinez Police said that a review of court records showed that Valdez was on pre-trial release for residential burglaries that happened on April 29 in Orinda. Police said the court records also show Valdez was taken into custody for allegedly violating a home detention monitoring rule on August 4, and then on August 5 (the day before the stabbing) he was released on his own recognizance and referred to home-detention monitoring. Contra Costa County records show Valdez is still in custody and his bail is set at more than $1 million. County records also show that Valdez was in a diversion program for a misdemeanor violation of a protective order. “What is so concerning is how could this individual, who was just released from custody with no known motive, now be allegedly involved with a vicious homicide?” said legal analyst and former prosecutor Steven Clark. “So, that’s something that people are going to look at: where did the system possibly go wrong in its evaluation of his risk to public safety prior to his continued release on home detention?” Clark continued. However, Clark noted that courts are required to find the least restrictive method for pre-trial detention. “There’s a delicate balance between public safety and the right of the individual for pre-trial release because they are presumed to be innocent,” explained Clark. Multiple neighbors on Francis Court described Stewart as a well-known and liked member of the neighborhood, who could often be seen doing home projects in his garage. Neighbors said that Stewart retired a few years ago and leaves behind a wife and two adult daughters. “He is a neighbor everybody wishes they had –that type of neighbor, very friendly, very helpful,” said Galina Pasternak who lives nextdoor to Stewart and his wife. Several neighbors who spoke with NBC Bay Area, including Pasternak, felt that Valdez should not have been released from custody. “It could have been prevented, if he was still behind bars, I would say ‘yes he should have been,’” she said. “And I’m glad he was arrested, thank you to the police who arrested him the next day very quickly, but it won’t bring Todd back,” Pasternak continued. Martinez police are still asking anyone with information about this case to get in touch with them. A photo provided by Martinez Police of the suspect in the deadly stabbing on August 6 at Francis Court. Photo Courtesy Martinez Police Facebook.
headlines.source: NBC Bay Area staff and Alyssa Goard

headlines.title: Caltrans to close eastbound lanes of Bay Bridge overnight through October
headlines.description: Caltrans will be blocking off four lanes of the Bay Bridge overnight, starting Monday and continuing through October. The closure is so that crews can paint the underside of the upper deck. It will affect eastbound traffic, from San Francisco to the East Bay. Typical closures will be from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. Sunday through Thursday. This is all part of a larger maintenance project that Caltrans will be working on for the next five years.

headlines.title: Woman struck by car driven by young boys in Oakland stabilized, friend says
headlines.description: A woman who was critically injured when she was struck by a car driven by two young children in Oakland has been stabilized at the hospital, a close friend said Friday. The collision happened at about 9:30 a.m. Thursday in the area of 35th and Mangels avenues, not far from Interstate 580, according to police. Security video captured a white Toyota, driven by two boys, who sources said are 6 and 4 years old, zoom by and out of frame toward Kiara Bowling and the dog. The Toyota struck another car before veering into Bowling and the dog and then crashing into a wall and fence. Bowling was taken to the hospital in critical condition, but her good friend, Jyorti Arora, provided a positive update on Friday. “I know we’re not out of the woods yet, but we all have a lot of faith,” Arora said. “She’s an incredibly strong woman, so we’re very grateful that all of her vitals are stable.” On Friday evening, Bowling’s aunt Karon Markham, who was part of the people who went to visit Bowling at Highland Hospital, added that “Kiara has a long road ahead of her. A lot of trauma to the brain, she has bleeding on the brain, she has fractures on her face and a fractured rib.” Bowling was caring for and walking Arora’s dog, Grizzly, when they were hit, Arora said. Grizzly was back home Friday after being treated for multiple injuries at an Oakland animal hospital. Her brother points out they are all still trying to recover from other family tragedies. “It’s been hard on all of us, because we recently had deaths over the recent years. The last two, regarding our mom and our brother. So, this on top of that, it’s had a huge impact on our family. So, we’re just hanging in there pulling through,” Donny, Bowling’s brother, said. Oakland Aug 6 Oakland Aug 7 Some people quickly called for parental accountability following the crash. “These parents need to be held responsible,” witness Lavelle Shah-Marquis said. “That was my main concern. These parents need to be held responsible.” It’s a unique legal question in a case involving drivers who are barely school-age and likely far too young to even face juvenile courts. “This is such a one-off,” legal analyst Steven Clark said. “I’ve never seen anything like this in my practice of 40 years.” Clark said the case may end up being handled by social services investigations and civil courts, not criminal courts. “There will be a level of accountability here civilly,” Clark said. “Certainly the insurance will likely step in and provide coverage for this tragic accident. A lot of questions are still left to be answered.” Clark said police likely will conduct interviews to see if there was a pattern of behavior not being addressed by the parents or if they were negligent in any way. Police said the parents were cooperating with their investigation. Arora said Bowling, if she could, would likely be an advocate for the two children. “She would advocate for their safety, wherever they are going to be the most safe,” Arora said. “That’s what she would advocate for. I know that in no part of her heart would she ever wish ill on them.” According to public records, Bowling is a noted community advocate for current and former foster kids in the East Bay and a winner of multiple Bay Area pageants. She was also an outstanding student at Cal State University East Bay.

headlines.title: ‘Magic baby': Smallest surviving baby born at a Walnut Creek hospital goes home
headlines.description: On Friday, the smallest surviving baby born at a Walnut Creek hospital finally went home with her family after a rough start in life. Weighing in at less than a pound, Baby Meadow is the smallest surviving baby born at John Muir Health’s Walnut Creek Medical Center. “Even saying a miracle seems like downplayed, she’s more than a miracle and I don’t really know the word for it yet, but it’s kind of like magic. She’s just a magic baby,” said her mother, Noel Creamer. Weighing just 350 grams, Meadow is the smallest surviving baby ever born at John Muir Health in Walnut Creek. She was so tiny, her outer layer of skin hadn’t yet developed so she was a different color and her eyes were fused closed. “It was almost like seeing a kitten, because kittens are born with their eyes closed. So, I kind of call her my little kitten,” Creamer said. Creamer says her baby had a condition that prevented her from getting the nutrients she needed while in the womb. The baby was so tiny Creamer says she was told by doctors at other medical facilities she had no chance at survival. “Even though she was so small, I felt her kick and move. And I just knew I knew she didn’t make it this far along for it just to be over,” Creamer said. That’s when she turned to doctors at John Muir Health, who said they had the technology and expertise to give her a fighting chance. After 167 days, mom got the green light to take Meadow home. The staff that’s cared for her for all these weeks lined up to celebrate and say goodbye to their tiniest patient ever. Her mom says she has lots of plans for her little girl, who until now hasn’t ventured outside. “I plan on taking her camping, that’s one of the first things we’ll do,” Creamer said.

headlines.title: Tens of thousands head to San Francisco for the 18th year of Outside Lands
headlines.description: San Francisco’s Outside Lands Music Festival kicked off its 18th year on Friday with the first day of the three day music festival. Friday was headlined by British pop star Charli XCX. Fans made their way by the tnes of thousands to see Charli XCX and the many other artists spread out across the festival’s seven stages. Organizers said this year’s event at Golden Gate Park was sold out. This festival is a test of the city’s transportation systems following major traffic issues on the Fourth of July that left people traveling by transit, rideshare, robotaxi, and car stranded for hours. The city urged people not to drive to the festival or park in nearby city streets. Instead, they encouraged fans to take special SFMTA shuttles straight to the festival entrance or the Judah Muni line which is walking distance from Golden Gate Park. The city also recommends attendees walk, bike, take e-bikes or scooters, or get a ride. There are designated rideshare drop-off and pick-up spots near the festival and Waymo rides are available in an area a few blocks away from the event. Traffic in the Richmond District following the festival Friday was slow but still moved forward, with crowds of attendees walking home and many using e-bikes and scooters to make their way through the city.

headlines.title: Federal court blocks Trump administration's new rules for homelessness funding
headlines.description: A Bay Area county says it has scored a legal victory in its lawsuit against the Trump administration, adding that Friday’s court ruling could help keep thousands of formerly homeless people housed, including children and older adults. The Trump administration previously announced new rules for how $4 billion in federal funding could be spent to combat homelessness across the country. But nonprofits and local governments — including Santa Clara County — argued those new restrictions would lead to dramatic cuts in funding for permanent housing, so they sued HUD. Friday, a federal court weighed in, ordering the Trump administration to throw out its new rules because HUD didn’t follow proper procedures in making the changes. Applications for the billions in funding were supposed to be due by the end of the month, but the ruling leaves homeless advocates wondering when a new application, and the billions in funding, will be released.
